selected_problem: Open-ended DWAC diagnosis observed historical evidence files in reverse filename order and applied a 96-row budget before considering Git revision freshness, so lexically later stale boundaries could starve newer main-line evidence and distort the next autonomous bottleneck selection.

execution.route_basis: single evidence-rich high-centrality autonomy diagnosis defect

changes: bridge/dwac_bridge.py now orders committed evidence files by their most recent Git revision before applying the truth-boundary row budget.
Evidence files absent from Git history remain observable and are placed ahead of committed history using deterministic mtime/path ordering.
Non-Git workspaces keep the prior deterministic reverse-filename fallback rather than claiming unavailable revision provenance.
A focused regression reproduces stale lexicographic starvation with 96 historical boundaries and proves that the newest committed boundary becomes visible and selected after the fix.

validation.pre_fix_regression: FAIL_AS_EXPECTED: selected historical boundary 0 MISSING instead of newest revision boundary

truth_boundaries: Git commit history is used as revision provenance only when the workspace provides it; non-Git workspaces retain the deterministic legacy fallback.
Tracked files modified after their last commit retain committed revision position; files absent from Git history are treated as current local evidence and ordered ahead by mtime/path.
This change fixes evidence observation freshness and does not claim that historical truth boundaries are semantically obsolete merely because they are older.
